recent_posts.title: The Future of Fauna
recent_posts.summary: Fauna announces the sunsetting of its service over the coming months due to financial challenges. Existing customers will be gradually transitioned off the service, with a commitment to open-sourcing Fauna's core database technology. This includes its unique transactional features, document-relational data model, and FQL database language, ensuring ongoing community value. The company expresses gratitude to its customers and partners, promising support throughout the migration process.

recent_posts.title: The Developer's Guide to Building with Fauna: From Local Testing to Production
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build and manage applications using Fauna, from defining schemas with Fauna Schema Language (FSL) to writing logic with Fauna Query Language (FQL) and user-defined functions (UDFs). Discover how to run Fauna locally using Docker, test your configurations, and integrate with continuous integration (CI) and continuous deployment (CD) pipelines using GitHub Actions. The guide emphasizes centralized logic, local development, schema migrations, and CI/CD integration for production-ready applications.

recent_posts.title: Scaling Reads and Writes without Managing Clusters
recent_posts.summary: Fauna eliminates the complexity of cluster management for scaling databases by providing a serverless solution that automatically handles consistency, scaling, and replication across multiple regions. This approach allows developers to focus on building features instead of managing infrastructure. The post explains setting up a database in Fauna, querying data, and connecting through code examples using Cloudflare Workers.

recent_posts.title: Fauna Event Feeds Now GA, Snapshot Export Available in Beta
recent_posts.summary: Fauna has announced that Event Feeds, a vital component of their change data capture capabilities, are now generally available for Pro and Enterprise customers. These feeds offer a persistent, queryable history of changes in a Fauna database, facilitating data synchronization, audit logging, and external system updates. Additionally, Fauna has introduced Snapshot Export in beta, enabling users to pull transactionally consistent snapshots for use with analytics platforms and search engines. The post includes a hands-on example of integrating Event Feeds into a serverless architecture using AWS Lambda and Fauna's Python driver.

recent_posts.title: Building Flexible, Dynamic Filters with the Fauna Query Language
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to create flexible, dynamic filters using the Fauna Query Language (FQL). This guide provides examples and insights on managing complex queries with dynamic criteria, elucidates the usage of Fauna client drivers, and offers solutions with JavaScript code snippets for building sophisticated search queries. It emphasizes enhancing code flexibility and maintainability.

recent_posts.title: The need for a truly serverless database in Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes excels in managing application components but struggles with integrating traditional databases due to their persistence, scaling, and manual provisioning requirements. A truly serverless database addresses these issues by aligning with modern development practices like Database as Code (DBaC), providing immediate availability, seamless scaling, and cost-efficient pricing. Such databases eliminate the need for vendor-specific configurations and focus on operational automation, ensuring strong data accuracy and consistent performance at any scale.

recent_posts.title: Fauna’s 2024 Product Recap
recent_posts.summary: Fauna's 2024 product recap includes introducing flexible and enforceable schema management, event streaming, and change data capture, deeper integration with Cloudflare Workers and Datadog, expansion into the Google Cloud and AWS Marketplace, and enhancements to the Fauna CLI with version 4.0.

recent_posts.title: How to Set Up a Continuous Deployment Pipeline for Your Serverless App
recent_posts.summary: Continuous deployment ensures faster feature delivery, consistent testing and validation, and routine deployments for serverless apps. By integrating database schema management into your CI/CD pipeline, you can handle all aspects of your serverless system efficiently. This guide provides a step-by-step process to set up a continuous deployment pipeline, covering tool selection, version control, automated tests, applying schema changes, ensuring zero-downtime migrations, and adding observability and monitoring. Tools like Fauna make this process easier with features like schema as code, CI/CD integration, zero-downtime migrations, and built-in validation.

recent_posts.title: How to maintain high availability in a multi-tenant SaaS app
recent_posts.summary: Ensuring high availability in multi-tenant SaaS applications is crucial for maintaining user satisfaction and preventing revenue loss. Techniques include solid architectural designs with scalable, fault-tolerant patterns, redundancy, automated failover systems, and security measures like attribute-based access control. Modern approaches involve serverless architectures and multi-region, multi-active database services. These strategies collectively enhance the system's resilience and reliability.

recent_posts.title: Fauna: The Truly Serverless Database
recent_posts.summary: Fauna offers a truly serverless database with features like immediate availability, seamless scaling, strong consistency, and low latency. It addresses challenges like cost inefficiency and inconsistent performance seen in traditional databases through a stateless HTTP API, multi-tenant clusters, and an innovative Calvin-based engine. Fauna eliminates deployment, infrastructure, and vendor-specific configurations, providing a predictable and reliable experience at any scale.
